description:
Test builds no longer produce incremental-compilation state by default, so a build that omits an environment override cannot fill the disk with it.

## Background

The workspace `Cargo.toml` declares `incremental = true` under both `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]`. Worker briefs ask for `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, but any invocation that misses the variable writes `target/<profile>/incremental` state. A sandboxed shell or a single `cargo doc` run is enough. On 2026-11-04 that state reached hundreds of gigabytes per worktree and spread through the shared worktree cache.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The workspace test profile does not enable incremental compilation, and its comment states why.
- [hard] REQ-02: A worker-style build and test run without `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` set (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`, then one targeted test) leaves zero bytes under `target/*/incremental` for workspace crates, measured from a clean target directory and reported with the measurement command.
- [hard] REQ-03: The build profile policy test asserts the profile setting, and the existing build-budget checks pass.
- [hard] REQ-04: `dev/TESTING.md` and the build-budget README describe the setting, with no remaining instruction that depends on remembering the environment variable.
title: Test builds produce no incremental-compilation state by default
